subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Can an attacker without the victim's authenticated WebSocket, gateway credential, or paired device key cause current main to accept or route a forged frame by predicting an event `seq` value or response `id`?
rationale: Current source separates event ordering from authorization and already enforces connection authentication, but only a security owner should conclusively reject the report or determine that a different transport-boundary threat remains.

options.title: Require a boundary-bypass PoC
options.body: Ask for a minimal two-client reproduction against current main and close as unsubstantiated if the unauthenticated client cannot affect the authenticated connection.

options.title: Sponsor defense-in-depth design
options.body: Define an explicit per-message integrity requirement only if the supported threat model must protect authenticated application frames independently of TLS or the established WebSocket connection.

recommendation.title: Require a boundary-bypass PoC
recommendation.body: Ask for a minimal two-client reproduction against current main and close as unsubstantiated if the unauthenticated client cannot affect the authenticated connection.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to the Gateway-backed SDK, client transport, and adjacent protocol boundary.
